chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to do a special thing for those who died from the Banu Hashim that he did not do for anyone else among the Muslims.
When he prayed over the Hashimi and sprinkled his grave with water, he would place his palm on the grave until his fingers were seen in the clay.

So the stranger would arrive or the traveler from the people of Medina, and he would see upon the new grave the mark of the palm of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and he would say, 'One from the family of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) has died.'

key_terms.الْهَاشِمِيِّ: The Hashimi (a member of the Banu Hashim clan)
key_terms.بَنِي هَاشِمٍ: Banu Hashim (the clan of Hashim, to which the Prophet belonged)

ai.seo_question: What special burial practice did the Prophet perform for the Banu Hashim clan?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the unique honor (*khasiyya*) bestowed upon the Banu Hashim, illustrating the Prophet’s personal affection and the distinct status of the Ahl al-Bayt within the early Muslim community. The physical mark left in the clay served not only as a practical identifier for travelers but also as a tangible sign of the Prophet’s enduring connection to his lineage, reinforcing the theological importance of the Prophet's family in Shia tradition.
